questions.q: In InvoiceHub, what is the tenant?
questions.explain: A tenant is one customer of the shared application, and InvoiceHub's customers are businesses. Users are global and can belong to several organizations, so they cannot be the tenant.
options: Each organization, such as Ada's Bakery

questions.q: Ada owns Ada's Bakery and is a viewer at Kola Motors. Where should her role be stored?
questions.explain: A role only means something together with an organization. The user row and the token have one role for all organizations, and a cookie is written by the client. The membership row is the only place where "owner of the bakery, viewer at Kola Motors" fits.
options: In a cookie the browser sends with each request

questions.q: Both organizations want their first invoice to be INV-0001. Which constraint is right?
questions.explain: Numbers are unique per organization, so the pair is unique. A global unique (number) would refuse Kola Motors' first invoice. Checking in code first has a race: two requests can both see "free" and both insert.
options: No constraint: check for duplicates in the code before inserting

questions.q: Why does invoices use foreign key (org_id, customer_id) references customers (org_id, id) instead of customer_id references customers (id)?
questions.explain: With the plain key, Kola Motors could bill the bakery's customer 1: that id exists. With the composite key the pair (kola-motors, 1) must exist, and it does not. The rule lives in the database, so no future code change can break it.
options: The database then refuses an invoice of one organization that points at another organization's customer
PostgreSQL does not allow single-column foreign keys on serial ids
It lets two customers share the same id

questions.q: Why does customers declare unique (org_id, id) although id is already its primary key?
questions.explain: PostgreSQL only accepts a foreign key whose target columns have a unique constraint or primary key as a group. The pair is trivially unique because id is, but it has to be declared.
options: To stop two organizations from having customers with the same name
A foreign key must point at columns declared unique together, and the invoice's composite key points at that pair

questions.q: InvoiceHub turned on row-level security, yet the seed code and db.query(...) outside inTenant still see every organization's rows. Why?
questions.explain: Table owners and superusers bypass policies. That is why inTenant switches to the ordinary role app_user, and why only migrations and seeds should ever run as the owner.
options: They run as the owner of the tables, and the owner (like any superuser) is not bound by the policies
PGlite does not support row-level security
The policy only applies after a restart

questions.q: A new route calls inTenant(db, "", …) by mistake: the organization id is empty. What does select * from invoices return inside it?
questions.explain: current_setting('app.org_id', true) returns an empty value instead of throwing, and no row has an empty org_id. The mistake fails closed: the client sees an empty list, not somebody else's data.
options: Every invoice, because the filter is empty
No rows: the policy compares org_id with an empty value and matches nothing
Only the invoices that have no organization

questions.q: Why does inTenant use set local role and set_config(..., true) inside a transaction, instead of a plain set once per connection?
questions.explain: With a connection pool, the next request that borrows the connection could be another tenant. A session-level setting would still say the previous organization. local scope ends at commit or rollback, so every transaction starts clean.
options: Plain set is not valid SQL in PostgreSQL
Local settings end with the transaction, so they cannot leak into the next request that reuses the same pooled connection
Local settings are faster to read
So that the seed data is also filtered

questions.q: A mobile developer asks to send the chosen organization in an x-tenant-id header on every request, "to save a database lookup". What is the problem?
questions.explain: Validating the format only proves the value looks like a tenant id. It says nothing about whether this user may use that organization. InvoiceHub takes the organization from a record the server wrote after checking the membership.
options: The client writes the header, so any logged-in user could name any organization; it is untrusted
Headers are not sent over HTTPS
There is no problem if the value is validated with tryCreateTenantId

questions.q: Why does InvoiceHub give every user roles: [] in the auth service, instead of putting their role in the login token?
questions.explain: "Owner" in a token does not say owner of what. And a demoted accountant would keep the old role for the token's whole lifetime. Reading the role from the membership row on every request fixes both.
options: The auth service does not support roles
Tokens with roles are larger than 8 KB
A token-wide role has no organization attached, and a role in a token cannot be revoked until the token expires
Roles in tokens are encrypted and cannot be read by the server

questions.q: The membership is checked at login. Why does loadMembership check it again on every request?
questions.explain: Tokens live for 15 minutes and sessions longer. The failure demo removed Bisi and promoted Tunde between two requests, and both changes applied at once, because the role is read from the database each time.
options: To make requests slower on purpose, as a rate limit
A member can be removed or demoted while their token and session are still valid; the next request must see that
Because the tenancy middleware forgets the organization

questions.q: Kola asks for GET /invoices/1, which belongs to Ada's Bakery. Which answer is best?
questions.explain: A 403 confirms that invoice 1 exists, which leaks information about another customer. For the attacker, "not yours" and "does not exist" must look the same.
options: 404 Not Found: the same answer as for an id that does not exist

questions.q: At login, a user names an organization they do not belong to. What should InvoiceHub answer when the organization exists, compared with when it does not?
questions.explain: Different answers would turn the login form into a way to discover which businesses use InvoiceHub. Ending the session means the refused login leaves nothing behind.
options: 404 when it does not exist, 403 when it exists
The same 403 in both cases, and the session that was just created is ended
A 200 with the list of organizations the user does belong to
A redirect to the organization's login page

questions.q: The engine has a global rule { effect: "deny", resource: "*", action: "*", condition: not(tenantIsolation("orgId", "orgId")) }. What happens when a route calls engine.can(actor, "invoice:create") with no resource?
questions.explain: Missing data means no. That is why every InvoiceHub check passes a resource, even for "create" and "list": { orgId: currentOrg().id }, the organization's collection.
options: Denied: tenantIsolation returns false when the resource is missing, so not(...) is true and the deny rule applies
Allowed, because deny rules only look at resources that exist

questions.q: Where must metadata.orgId in the permission check come from?
questions.explain: The deny rule compares the resource's organization with the request's organization. If the request's side came from the client or from the resource itself, the comparison would prove nothing.
options: The tenant context, which the server set from the verified session

questions.q: Why does InvoiceRepository.list() take no orgId parameter?
questions.explain: A parameter can be filled from the wrong place, such as the query string. The context is set once, by the middleware, from a trusted source. Outside a context the repository throws TenantContextMissingError.
options: Because the invoices table has no org_id column
It reads the organization from the tenant context, so a caller has nothing to pass and nothing to get wrong
Because PostgreSQL adds the filter automatically without a policy

questions.q: Why does InvoiceHub use namespace: orgId with @zudojs/cache instead of a key from tenantKey(tenantId, "dashboard.totals")?
questions.explain: The cache uses : to separate prefix, namespace and key, so it refuses it inside a key part. A tenant id is a valid namespace, because both allow only letters, digits, - and _.
options: tenantKey builds tenant:kola-motors:dashboard.totals, and the cache refuses keys that contain a colon

questions.q: The founders want "bulk reminders" for about 10% of organizations. Which evaluation context is right?
questions.explain: The percentage rule buckets by userId first, then tenantId, then sessionId. With the user in the context, members of one organization land in different buckets and disagree. For an organization feature, leave the user out.

questions.q: Why does POST /reminders/bulk answer 404 for an organization outside the beta, rather than 403?
questions.explain: Unreleased features often carry names you have not announced. The route still checks invoice:send after the flag: a flag is not a permission.
options: A feature that is not released should look like one that does not exist; 403 would say "this exists, but not for you"
Because the flag store threw an error
Because the route has no permission check

questions.q: InvoiceHub sets notFoundResponse on the tenancy middleware so that an unknown, a suspended and a "no longer a member" organization all answer 404 Organization not found. What does that protect?
questions.explain: Different messages ("Tenant not found" from the middleware, "Organization not found" from loadMembership) would let anyone with a token probe the state of other organizations. The owner of a suspended organization learns why by e-mail, not from a 404.
options: A caller cannot learn from the API which organizations exist or which are suspended
It stops the suspended organization's owner from logging in
It lets the cache store the error

questions.q: A nightly job must e-mail every organization's overdue invoices. Which design keeps isolation?
questions.explain: Inside tenantContext.run the job uses the same two walls as a request. One big owner query puts every organization's rows in one loop, where one bug (or one log line) mixes them up.
options: Run select * from invoices where status = 'sent' once as the table owner and group the rows in code
Pass the organization id in an x-tenant-id header to the API
Loop over the organizations and, for each one, call tenantContext.run(org, …) and use the repository
Turn off row-level security for the job's transaction

questions.q: The isolation test starts with expect(ids.length).toBeGreaterThan(0). Why?
questions.explain: If a seed change left the victim without invoices, the attack loop would never run, and the suite would still be green. The guard makes that situation fail loudly.
options: To make Vitest count the test as passed
A loop over an empty list of victim ids would pass without testing anything
Because Vitest fails on empty arrays

questions.q: Why does the "never lists or counts" test load the victim's dashboard before the attacker's?
questions.explain: The caching leak depends on order: whoever fills the shared key first decides what everybody sees. The test creates exactly that order, and the mutation run showed it fail when namespace was removed.
options: A cache keyed without the tenant only leaks when another organization filled the entry first; testing one tenant at a time never shows it
Because the dashboard route needs a warm-up request

questions.q: Someone removes both the org_id filter and inTenant from InvoiceRepository.get. Kola requests the bakery's invoice 1. What happens, and why does the test still fail?
questions.explain: The deny rule is a third wall: the foreign invoice is loaded but refused. The answer is still wrong, because it tells the attacker that invoice 1 exists, and the suite catches it.
options: 200 with the invoice; the test fails because the body contains the bakery's orgId
403 from the permission engine's same-org-only rule; the test fails because it expects 404, and a 403 confirms the invoice exists
500, because the query has no parameters

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The key has no organization in it. Kola Motors filled invoices.count first with 1, and the bakery was served that entry. Add { namespace: orgId }.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The full key is prefix:namespace:key, with the default prefix zudojs. The same key in another namespace is a different entry, so the bakery gets a miss.

questions.q: After a new invoice, this code clears the bakery's dashboard. What does it print?
questions.explain: Tags live inside a namespace. Without the namespace, nothing matches and nothing is cleared, silently. That is why invoicesChanged() takes the namespace from the tenant context, like the read does.

questions.q: A developer builds cache keys by joining the organization and the key with a colon. What does this print?
questions.explain: Two different (organization, key) pairs produce the same string, so one can read or overwrite the other's entry. That is why @zudojs/cache refuses : inside key parts and tenant ids only allow letters, digits, - and _.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The first check is her own organization. The second is another organization's invoice: the deny rule wins over invoice:*. The third has no orgId in the metadata, so tenantIsolation cannot confirm a match and the deny rule applies: missing data means no.

questions.q: Roles come from a memberships table. What does this print?
questions.explain: The same person gets a different actor in each organization. With no membership, the actor has no roles, and everything is denied by default.
options:
adas-bakery true
kola-motors false
chidi-pharmacy false

adas-bakery true
kola-motors true
chidi-pharmacy false

adas-bakery true
kola-motors true
chidi-pharmacy true

adas-bakery true
kola-motors false
chidi-pharmacy true

questions.q: The flag rolls out to 10%. The bakery's bucket for this flag is 337, Ada's is 2129 (a bucket below 1000 is inside 10%). What does this print?
questions.explain: The percentage rule buckets by userId when there is one, and only falls back to tenantId without it. Adding the user changed the subject from the bakery (in) to Ada (out).

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: enabled: false is the kill switch: the flag ignores its rules and serves its off value, even for the pilot organization.

questions.q: The isolation test's helper finds every orgId in a response body. What does this print?
questions.explain: Searching the JSON text finds the nested customer too. A test that only compared the top-level orgId would miss this leak.

questions.q: A repository is written two ways. What does this print?
questions.explain: Looking up by id alone returns another organization's invoice. Putting the organization in the lookup itself makes a foreign id behave exactly like a missing one.

questions.q: InvoiceHub numbers invoices per organization. What does this print?
questions.explain: Each organization has its own sequence, and padStart(4, "0") pads to four digits. A new organization starts at 1. In the database, unique (org_id, number) backs this up.

questions.q: This sketch mimics the tenant context with a variable that a run function sets and restores. What does it print?
questions.explain: Inside run the organization is set; after it, it is restored to "none", and code that needs a tenant fails loudly. A plain variable breaks as soon as two requests overlap across an await, which is why the real context uses AsyncLocalStorage.

questions.q: Write orgTotals(orgId) that returns the organization's invoice count through cache.getOrSet, loading it from countInDb, so that each organization gets its own entry. Print the bakery's count, Kola Motors' count, and then the bakery's again with whether it came from the cache.
questions.explain: The namespace puts the organization into the key, so Kola Motors misses and loads its own count instead of receiving the bakery's cached one.

questions.q: Write sameOrg(resource, orgId) for a hand-written check. It returns true only when both the resource's orgId and the given orgId are present and equal. Missing data on either side must mean false. Print the four cases.
questions.explain: The third case is the classic bug: undefined === undefined is true, so a naive comparison lets a request with no organization read every row that has none. Check that both values exist first, as tenantIsolation does.

questions.q: Write a createInvoiceRepository(rows, currentOrg) factory whose list() and get(id) only ever return rows of currentOrg(); outside an organization (currentOrg() returns undefined) both must throw "no tenant". Print the list for Kola Motors, then get(1) for Kola Motors, then the error message outside a tenant.
questions.explain: The organization is read inside every method, from one trusted source, and callers never pass it. A foreign id comes back as undefined, which the API turns into a 404.
questions.expected:
[ { id: 3, orgId: 'kola-motors', number: 'INV-0001' } ]
undefined
no tenant

questions.q: Write orgFlagContext(org) that returns an evaluation context for an organization-level feature: the organization's id and its plan as an attribute, and no user. Then print whether priority-support is on for each organization. The flag is on for organizations on the pro plan.
questions.explain: The plan comes from the organization row on the server, never from the request. Without a userId, any percentage rule you add later buckets by the organization as well.

questions.q: Write loginDecision(memberships, userId, org) for the login route. It returns { status: 200, role } when the user is a member of org, and otherwise exactly { status: 403, error: "You are not a member of that organization" }, whether or not the organization exists. Print three cases as JSON.
questions.explain: The decision never looks at whether the organization exists, so the two refusals are identical and the login form reveals nothing about other customers.

questions.q: Build a permission engine with the roles viewer (invoice:read) and accountant (inherits viewer, plus invoice:create), and a deny rule named same-org-only that refuses any permission on a resource of another organization, using not and tenantIsolation("orgId", "orgId"). Print the three checks shown in the starter.
questions.explain: Roles answer "may this person do this kind of thing here?", and the deny rule answers "is this thing from here at all?". Both must say yes.

questions.q: Write checkIsolation(responses, attacker). responses is a list of { label, status, body } that a member of attacker received while probing another organization's ids. It returns the labels that failed: any status other than 404, or any orgId in the body (at any depth) that is not attacker. Print the result.
questions.explain: The 403 confirms the invoice exists, and the second 404 still carries the victim's organization in a nested field. Both are leaks; a check on the status alone would catch only one of them.

questions.q: Use isInRollout(flagKey, subject, percentage) from @zudojs/feature-flags to count how many of 1,000 organizations (org-0 to org-999) are inside a 10% rollout of bulk-reminders, and print whether the count is between 80 and 120.
questions.explain: Bucketing is deterministic, so the same organizations are in every time, and the share is close to the percentage. Printing a range instead of the exact number keeps the check about the idea, not about one hash function.
questions.starter:
import { isInRollout } from "@zudojs/feature-flags";

// count org-0 … org-999 inside a 10% rollout of "bulk-reminders"
